A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, algorithms, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees and proofs, schematic learning illustrations, and astronomical examples attributed to other sources. It contains no original empirical evaluation.

after.justification: v2 adds original synthetic-data experiments in Section 4. Figure 3 reports convergence results for four methods, aggregated over ten repetitions.

M1.justification: Algorithm 3 changes the number of discarded intervals from (k−1)/ε to (k−1)/(εs)^q. Algorithm 2 similarly changes its iteration count from 1/ε to (εs)^(−q). These are actual corrections to smoothness-dependent procedure parameters; the overall set-learning and PSGD architecture is retained.

E1.justification: v1 has no evaluated datasets. v2 introduces empirical coverage through synthetic truncated linear regression with ten-dimensional features drawn from a five-component Gaussian mixture and a survival set comprising five intervals. This establishes the paper's first empirical test setting.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Figure 3 introduce comparisons against OLS and two versions of PSGD attributed to Daskalakis et al. [DGTZ19], supplied either an incorrect or the true truncation set. These methods were not empirically compared in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a convergence evaluation measuring Euclidean parameter error against iteration, with R=10 identified in Figure 3 and controls using correct versus incorrect truncation information. This is a new evaluation design, rather than a revision or rerun of an existing v1 experiment.

E4.justification: The new simulation includes a limited diagnostic of truncation misspecification: PSGD with an incorrect survival set is compared with exact-set PSGD and the full algorithm. This examines the importance of estimating the set correctly, but adds no broader sensitivity sweep or robustness suite.

E5.justification: Figure 3 newly reports ten experiment repetitions, plotting mean Euclidean error with standard-deviation shading. v1 contains no empirical repeated-run or uncertainty reporting. The addition is confined to this single simulation.

E6.justification: Figure 3 supplies the first empirical results: the full algorithm's error decreases nearly alongside exact-set PSGD, while OLS remains substantially biased and incorrect-set PSGD retains much larger error. These are newly reported convergence findings, not performance gains over corresponding v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The interval-count guarantee in v1 Theorem 3.3, now Theorem 3.4, changes to (k−1)/(εs)^q+1. Related bounds and proofs in Appendix D.1 and runtime guarantees in Corollaries D.14, D.18 and D.19 are revised to include parameter-dependent exponents. Section 3.3 also corrects the duplicated known-set likelihood formula. These are localized mathematical corrections; the main theorem and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: polynomial-time regression with unknown outcome truncation under sub-Gaussian features, supported by efficient positive-only learning of unions of intervals. The added simulation does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.2 explains the additional sample-complexity dependence through the precision required when learning the survival set. Section 4 also qualifies exact-set PSGD as an idealized comparator unavailable when the set is unknown, clarifying how to interpret the empirical comparison.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds a simulation-code repository link and a brief description of the synthetic setup, neither present in v1. Reproducibility information remains limited within the PDFs: sample counts, mixture parameters, interval endpoints and experiment-specific optimizer settings are not specified.

R1.justification: Remark B.2 expands the comparison with Lee, Mehrotra and Zampetakis [LMZ24], explicitly stating that its computational cost persists for product survival sets. An introduction footnote foregrounds the scope distinction already discussed in v1's appendix. This is a focused refinement of research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a simulations section before the conclusion, adds Remark 3.2, expands selected appendix explanations, and makes notation and cross-reference edits. The existing introduction, theoretical narrative and appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the convergence plot with uncertainty shading as Figure 3; the retained astronomical photograph becomes Figure 4. Existing explanatory diagrams are relocated, Figure 2's caption specifies s=q=1, and bibliography text is enlarged. These are limited additions and layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: Restoring smoothness dependence in the algorithms and corresponding appendix bounds improves internal consistency, although some auxiliary guarantees become less favorable. The ten-run simulation and code pointer add useful empirical support. The main theoretical contribution remains unchanged, and the empirical addition covers only one incompletely specified synthetic setting, so the overall improvement is limited.
